title: Automate profile publish and lifecycle playbook for Redwood-verified performance profiles
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create an automated, auditable pipeline and operational playbook to publish and maintain Redwood-verified performance profiles (latency/throughput/cost) for onboarded models. This covers initial profiling runs, version pinning metadata, publishing to the catalog, scheduled reprofiles, rollback/retirement flows, and integration with Console and SDKs.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible CI job (profile-runner) that produces a signed performance profile JSON and stores it in S3 + metadata in the profiles DB
A lightweight web UI in Console showing profile provenance, last-run, drift delta, and one-click pin/unpin
Publish step creates immutable release entry with version tag and model variant mapping; SDKs can pin to specific profile versions
Automated daily smoke reprofile for high-traffic models and weekly for long-tail models with alerting on >10% latency/cost regression
Rollback/retire flow that marks profiles deprecated and triggers SDK & routing policy fallbacks
Security review completed for signing keys and upload permissions
notes: We will leverage existing verified-bench pipeline but need to add signing and metadata standardization (profile_version, commit_sha, runner_image, sampling_config)
Trade-off: full determinism requires locking model weights, env, and tokenization; we will record environment fingerprint instead of attempting byte-for-byte reproducibility
We should prioritize automating profiles for top-20 models by traffic first to reduce manual load
Cost: initial CI infra to run profiling on ≤2k tokens per model will be ~monthly $Xk; see cost estimate in the linked doc
Assumed prerequisites: model onboarding checklist completed (data access, licensed model artifact, legal signoff where required)
